note: PLUGIN-005 cancel external action: asking a plugin to stop is not the same as it having stopped, so src/plugin/cancellation.zig makes cancellation a state the action passes through rather than one it lands in. The lease is held through cancelling and releaseLease refuses while the action is not terminal, because a lease released early is a working directory that can be collected while a process still writes to it - the cancellation causing the corruption it was meant to prevent. Only evidence that the process tree is gone makes the action terminal, and a plugin that never acknowledges leaves the action cancelling with its lease held, because that is what is known; nothing is guessed to make the bookkeeping tidier. Reaping an action that was never cancelling is refused so this cannot become a general-purpose status setter, cancelling an already-terminal action is refused so a completed action cannot be rewritten as cancelled, and releasing a lease that is not held is distinguished from releasing too early. Fault proof: dropping the terminal-state requirement lets the lease go while the tree runs and the refusal assertion fails (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
